# Working with OpenAPI definition

## Shape
- 25 read operations, 27 write operations.
- Collections paginate. Follow the pagination fields rather than guessing offsets.
- Nested objects are sometimes returned as bare ids; fetch them, or use `expand` where offered.

## Reads
- `read_target_contract` — GET /api/v1/targets/{id}/contract
- `get_artifact` — GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{*name}
- `read_pack` — GET /api/v1/packs/{id}
- `get_experiment` — GET /api/v1/experiments/{id}
- `list_targets` — GET /api/v1/targets
- `list_runs` — GET /api/v1/runs
- `list_experiments` — GET /api/v1/experiments
- `get` — GET /artifacts/{runId}/{*path}
- …and 17 more; search or describe to find them.

## Writes

The same change may be reachable several ways. They are not equivalent: a full replace drops fields you did not send, and action endpoints may be irreversible. Prefer the narrowest operation that does what you were asked.

- `write_target_contract` — PUT /api/v1/targets/{id}/contract
- `put_artifact` — PUT /api/v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{*name}
- `write_pack` — PUT /api/v1/packs/{id}
- `delete_pack` — DELETE /api/v1/packs/{id}
- `update_experiment` — PUT /api/v1/experiments/{id}
- `delete_experiment` — DELETE /api/v1/experiments/{id}
- `upsert_provider` — PUT /api/v1/config/providers/{id}
- `delete_provider` — DELETE /api/v1/config/providers/{id}
